answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk at 94% utilization with zero buffer and a primary contract that dies in 14 days (no auto-renew). A broad primary switch would meet the 18% mandate on unit price but is an unbuffered cutover; c2’s ‘quick onboarding’ is load-bearing and may not transfer, so it must be verified rather than treated as settled. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so renew-as-is fails TCO and a second negotiate may also fail—but expiry is a true renewal point, c4 says benchmarking at renewal moved price and terms, and the low-cost quote is that benchmark. Verify c4/c2 before committing. c5 does not apply (critical line, no month-to-month). Dual-source cannot also solve the expiring primary in a one-decision cycle.
